reader.requirement: At --std 85 a file description entry must accept REPORT [IS] or REPORTS [ARE] followed by one or more report-names, in any order (XIII.3.3.3 SR1), and produce each named report on that file (GR1); a mismatched optional word (REPORT ARE, REPORTS IS), an empty name list, a name that is no RD, a report named twice and the clause written twice must be refused. The witness covers two reports sharing one file.
reader.edition-search: grep reportClause() across the compiler (two sites, FileControlBinder.FileSection.cs, neither edition-switched); grep Edition.DialectLevel/Edition.Edition.Year/Constructs in ResolveReports (its only edition reads, SubscriptedClauseOperands and DialectLevel>=2002, serve the CONTROL clause, not the REPORT clause); VersionConformancePass has no VisitReportClause
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the same grammar rule and name resolution at 85 and 2023 (p6b prints the same report at both)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness exercises REPORTS sharing a file; the optional-word omissions, the singular keyword with several names, and the refusals are not exercised

reader.notes: The grammar (REPORT IS? | REPORTS ARE?) reportName+ is exactly the 1985 format, and the FD binder plus ResolveReports bind each name to its RD with SR1/SR2 enforced; no edition is consulted and none needs to be. The FD member is the clause loop inside FileControlBinder.FileSection.cs (the reportClause arm).

refuter.evidence: At --std 85, against SR3 and the file's open modes the reader did not probe: q1 FD RFILE REPORTS ARE R1 R2, OPEN OUTPUT / INITIATE R1 R2 / GENERATE D1 / TERMINATE / CLOSE, then OPEN EXTEND (legal per SR3) / INITIATE R2 / GENERATE D2 -> 'EXT FS=00', file 'R1 / R2' (extend appended); q2 OPEN INPUT RFILE -> COBOL2371; q3 OPEN I-O RFILE -> COBOL2371; q4 READ RFILE -> COBOL2577 (SR3). Class c: q5 report-name TYPEDEF (not reserved in 1985) in REPORTS ARE TYPEDEF R2 -> runs at 85, refused COBOL0901 at --std 2023. cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.3.3.3 SR3 the text is in SR3 (and the reader's SR1, SR2, GR1 lines stand).
